answer: Like a harbor admitting only ships with proven cargo logs, an agent economy can demand a costly, verifiable work trail before granting trade rights: each identity must post a bonded stake locked in an escrow contract that is slashed on fraud. Attackers spawning a gale of raven-named throwaway accounts find every new hull costs real capital, so mass-forging identities bleeds money faster than honest work earns. Legitimate agents accumulate reputation that lowers their future transaction costs, while sybils start at zero and pay full price every time.
